items.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: And he told me who was in the band, he said Davy Tough, Max Kaminsky, Claude Thornhill and Sam Donahue. And it sounded like a good group, which it was

ctx.x: Oh, that’s true, yeah. Well what happened to you during the war years? What was your experience during World War II?

Mine? Well I survived for one thing. I didn’t want to get drafted. After the Miller band broke up, in September of ‘42, in Passaic, New Jersey, I joined the Bob Crosby band. And that lasted six weeks and that band broke up at that time. In the meantime during that period I got a call from Artie Shaw, that he was recruiting a band of professional musicians for the Navy. And their job would be to play for the troops, the military, as close to the action of the war as they would send us. And he told me who was in…

and stay — Shaw was discharged. They threatened to break the band up then and send us out as replacements. But somebody in Washington said keep the group together, you’ve got an excellent group. So Sam Donahue was the leader. They sent us to England for a year, and that’s where we had battle music with Glenn’s Army band, on the Londonderry Club in London. The Queensbury Club, I said Londonderry, Queensbury.
